book_title: Chapter 3: From Petrochemical Chips to Global Tint Bays — Unit Economics & Cash Flow
question: How does GHFL move specialty films from Aurangabad to 90+ countries, what does its ₹100 revenue waterfall actually keep as free cash flow, and why is inventory rising even as debtors stay near zero?

epigraph.quote: Vertical integration lowers unit cost in booms, but its true test is working-capital discipline when export channels pause to destock.
epigraph.author: Supply Chain Audit Principle

web_blocks.title: 3.1 Global Distribution Architecture: US Subsidiary, Regional Dealers & 250+ Studios

web_blocks.html: GHFL earns roughly 74–75% of its sales from exports across 90+ countries and 25–26% in India [10, 16]. The United States is its top overseas market at ~51% of total sales [10]. Europe adds 12–15%, while the Middle East and rest of world bring 10–12% [10]. In North America and Europe, GHFL sells through its wholly owned US unit, Global Hi-Tech Films [16]. Based in Tampa, Florida, that unit markets under Global Window Films and uses regional dealers to reach tint bays and glaziers [16]. In India, consumer brand trust drives sales. GHFL has built 250+ Garware Application Studios (GAS) and Garware Home Solutions outlets [4, 11, 15]. Its Waluj and Chikalthana plants also act as training hubs to certify installers on dust-free PPF and building films [4, 11, 15].

web_blocks.title: 3.2 Raw Material Supply Chain & Backward Integration into TPU

web_blocks.html: Upstream, GHFL's polyester film lines use petrochemical feedstocks—Purified Terephthalic Acid (PTA) and Monoethylene Glycol (MEG). Its 66,000 MT chips plant polymerizes both inputs in-house [4, 17]. Until now, however, its fast-growing PPF business had to import Thermoplastic Polyurethane (TPU) base film. That left GHFL exposed to foreign polymer suppliers, currency swings, and ocean freight delays. In FY25–FY27, GHFL tackled this gap by teaming up with global chemical leader Lubrizol [5, 6, 11]. Together they built a ~₹118 Cr platform to launch India's first 360 LSF TPU extrusion line in Q3 FY27 [5, 6, 11]. At the same time, GHFL petitioned India's Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) and won anti-dumping duty backing against cheap Chinese TPU PPF imports [14].

web_blocks.title: 3.3 Working Capital Paradox: 9-Day Receivables vs. 149-Day Inventory

web_blocks.html: A close look at GHFL's cash cycle shows a sharp split. Indian studios and global dealers pay quickly or against letters of credit, keeping Debtor Days at just 7–9 days (9 days in FY26, down from 26 days in FY17) [1]. Yet Inventory Days rose from 116 days in FY25 to 149 days in FY26 [1]. That pushed the Cash Conversion Cycle to 89 days, up from 68 days in FY25 and 54 days in FY21 [1]. Two structural drivers explain this build. First, GHFL stocks finished rolls in US and European depots for 48-hour delivery to tint shops. Second, it holds raw-material and WIP buffers across thousands of tint and PPF shades. Management noted that net working capital tightened back to 29 days in H1 FY27 as Q1–Q2 shipments surged [11].

web_blocks.takeaway: Out of every ₹100 of FY26 revenue, GHFL converted ₹20.52 into core operating profit, ₹15.94 into net profit, ₹12.97 into operating cash flow (after inventory expansion), and ₹5.38 into free cash flow after funding ₹161 Cr of growth capex internally [1, 9].

web_blocks.title: Tariff & Trade-Policy Chokepoint: 51% U.S. Exposure
paragraphs: While GHFL successfully secured successor-in-interest status in its U.S. Department of Commerce Changed Circumstances Review for PET film anti-dumping orders [13], having ~51% of consolidated revenue tied to the United States leaves quarterly shipments vulnerable to broader U.S. tariff shifts and distributor pre-buying/destocking cycles [10, 22].

web_blocks.title: 3.4 Feedstock Sensitivity: PTA/MEG Cyclicality vs. Global Sourcing

web_blocks.html: GHFL makes its own polyester chips from PTA and MEG. Raw material costs came to ₹917.85 Cr (43.3% of sales) in FY26, down slightly from ₹934.78 Cr (44.3% of sales) in FY25 [9]. Sharp oil or chemical swings can briefly lag price pass-through in the 25% Industrial Product Division. Even so, GHFL's global supplier base and 75% high-margin CPD mix shield gross margins far better than pure packaging-film peers [4, 10, 22].

book_paragraphs: To understand how a factory in Aurangabad earns 20% to 28% operating margins selling polymer films into Texas and Dubai, you and I have to trace the supply chain from raw petrochemical molecules to the installer's squeegee. Roughly 74% to 75% of Garware's revenue comes from exports across more than 90 countries, with the United States alone accounting for about 51% of total sales, Europe contributing 12% to 15%, and the Middle East and other markets adding another 10% to 12%.

In the United States, Garware operates through its subsidiary Global Hi-Tech Films in Tampa, Florida, selling to regional distributors and independent tint shops under the Global Window Films name. In India, where consumers recognize the Garware name directly, the company has rolled out more than 250 Garware Application Studios. That retail studio network solves a critical industry problem: even the best 8-mil Paint Protection Film looks terrible if applied in a dusty roadside garage. By training and certifying applicators inside its Waluj and Chikalthana plants, Garware protects both its brand reputation and installer economics.

Upstream, the company's 66,000-ton chips plant converts PTA and MEG into proprietary polyester resins, shielding it from merchant film volatility. Until recently, however, its fast-growing PPF vertical still had to import Thermoplastic Polyurethane base films. That is why the Lubrizol partnership and the ₹118 crore, 360-lakh-square-foot TPU extrusion line commissioning in Q3 FY27 matter so much: once running, Garware will control the core TPU extrusion step inside India, cutting import dependence and capturing another layer of manufacturing margin.

Now look at the unit economics through our FY26 ₹100 revenue waterfall. Out of every ₹100 Garware billed in FY26—on ₹2,120 crore of consolidated sales—direct materials and manufacturing inputs consumed about ₹47.94, employee costs took ₹7.56, and power, freight, and overhead took ₹23.97. That left ₹20.52 of core operating profit. After ₹2.12 for depreciation, just ₹0.38 for interest, ₹3.07 of treasury income, and ₹5.09 of taxes, Garware kept ₹15.94 as net profit. Notice how clean the receivables side is: debtor days sit at just 9 days because international distributors and studios settle quickly. Yet cash from operations came in at ₹12.97 per ₹100 of sales, because inventory days stretched from 116 to 149 days to buffer overseas warehouses and specialty SKUs. Even after reinvesting ₹7.59 per ₹100 of sales into growth capex, Garware still generated ₹5.38 of pure free cash flow—funding its expansion entirely out of internal accruals.

book_subsections.title: Why 149 Inventory Days Happened—And Why Receivables Stayed at 9 Days
paragraphs: Whenever you see inventory days jump from 116 to 149 days in a single fiscal year, your first instinct should be to ask whether unsold goods are piling up because customers stopped buying. Here, the forensic clue lies in the contrast with debtor days: receivables remained rock-solid at 7 to 9 days, meaning customers who took delivery paid almost immediately.

The inventory build reflects two realities of running a global specialty film hub from India. First, a tint shop in Florida will not wait six weeks for a container from Mumbai; Garware has to hold finished rolls across dozens of tint shades and widths in overseas warehouses for 48-hour fulfillment. Second, when U.S. tariff headlines caused dealers to pause orders in late FY26, stock sat temporarily in the pipeline—before normalizing rapidly to 29 days of net working capital in H1 FY27 as export shipments surged.

On the cost side, raw materials consumed ₹917.85 crore in FY26, or roughly 43.3% of revenue, down slightly from ₹934.78 crore in FY25. Because Garware buys PTA and MEG across a diversified global supplier network and converts most of that polymer into branded consumer films rather than commodity wrap, petrochemical swings rarely derail consolidated margins.

Still, you and I must keep one eye on that 51% U.S. revenue concentration. Even with a wholly owned Tampa subsidiary and clean U.S. Department of Commerce anti-dumping standing, any broad U.S. tariff escalation on Indian industrial exports forces either temporary price absorption or distributor hesitation—exactly what we saw in the flat top-line of FY26.

book_callouts.title: Watch Inventory Days Alongside Margins
book_callouts.text: Debtor days of 7–9 days prove customer quality, but 149 inventory days in FY26 show that overseas warehousing and SKU breadth tie up working capital whenever U.S. demand pauses.
